si.t: MBody AI Orchestrator - Onboarding Data Request Map
Source: Chris's v1.1 onboarding HTML, flattened. Built 28 Apr 26. Customer: Mohegan (next deployment).
Q1 = Pre-deploy questionnaire | Q2 = Post-deploy questionnaire (+2 weeks) | Priority = how blocking this is for go-live
Frames the entire deployment narrative. Tells Chris what 'success' looks like for this customer so dashboards and benchmarks are calibrated to their goal (labour saved, hygiene, audit scores, etc.).
Customer-specific - cannot dummy. Sales picks up during deal phase per prior session.
Baseline annual cost of manual operations replaced ($)
Anchor for FTE/labour savings ROI. Without baseline we cannot calculate or report savings.
Standing assumption: $17/hr + 20% overhead. Use as dummy if customer can't supply.
Sets the savings target Orchestrator will measure against. Used in Breakeven Trend report.
Time horizon for ROI realisation. Drives expectations and reporting cadence around when savings should appear.
Captures secondary ROI: hygiene scores, audit pass rates, staff injury reduction, 24/7 coverage.
How ROI will be measured & reported
Defines the methodology so finance and ops both agree on the math at QBR time.
Use standard MBody methodology as dummy.
Target sq ft cleaned per robot per day
Standing assumption: 8 hrs/day utilization x robot speed.
Target utilization hours per robot per day
Same productivity benchmark expressed in hours. Defaults to 8 hrs/day.
KPI selection (which of the 10 standard KPIs to track)
Determines what the dashboard shows and what alerts fire. Sales proposes the set, customer confirms.
Default to all 10 standard KPIs as dummy until customer narrows.
The single metric that goes top-and-centre on the dashboard. Forces customer to pick what matters most.
Default to Avg Coverage as dummy headline.
Tells Orchestrator when to push reports. Default: real-time + daily + weekly + monthly.
Some customers want bespoke metrics. Captures the formula so Chris's team can build it.
Park to Q2 unless customer raises it. Default: none.
Defines what 'green / amber / red' means on the dashboard.
Use industry benchmarks as dummy targets; refine post-deploy.
Confirm total robot count in Orchestrator
Catches data ingestion errors before go-live. Customer compares Orchestrator count to physical asset list.
Confirm robot models / types are correct
Wrong model means wrong reporting benchmarks (SP50 vs L3 vs L4 have different specs).
Makes sure no property is missing from Orchestrator.
Confirm floors / zones mapped correctly per site
Each robot operates in a defined zone. Mislabelled zones = wrong reporting attribution.
Initial map from floor plan pre-deploy; final on Day 1.
Customer's reporting hierarchy (e.g. Site A floors 1-3 = 'North Wing'). Drives roll-ups.
Floor plans (CAD, image, or written description)
Source of truth for mapping zones, no-go areas, charging stations.
Areas with names + size + floor type + cleaning hours
Structured area inventory. Drives schedule generation and route planning.
Estimate from floor plan as dummy; refine on Day 1.
Restricted zones (gaming floor, VIP suites, maintenance areas)
No-go zone list. Critical for casino floor where regulator may prohibit robots near tables.
Robot register validation (per robot: ID, correct Y/N, amendment)
Line-by-line audit of robot records. Catches typos, mis-serials, duplicates.
Single capture field for any corrections found during validation.
Empty by default; populated as issues found.
Executive sponsor / owner (fleet-wide) - name, title, email, mobile
Top-of-house signoff, escalation point of last resort, QBR attendee.
Cannot dummy a real contact. Capture shift availability + alert tier (P1/P2/P3) for alert recipients.
Operations director (fleet-wide) - name, title, email, mobile
Owns the deployment outcome day-to-day across properties.
Robot programme manager (fleet-wide) - name, title, email, mobile
MBody's main point of contact on the customer side. Owns schedules, zones, KPI tuning.
Finance & reporting contact (fleet-wide) - name, title, email, mobile
Receives ROI reports and validates savings claims.
IT / network contact (fleet-wide) - name, title, email, mobile
Owns WiFi, VLAN, firewall, and any IT-side integrations.
Site manager (per location) - name, title, email, mobile
Property-level owner. First responder for non-emergency issues.
Cleaning / ops supervisor (per site) - name, title, email, mobile
Day-to-day operator. Knows the schedule, zones, staff workflow.
Health & safety officer (per site) - name, title, email, mobile
Owns H&S risk for guests and staff around robots.
First responder - robot incidents (per site, 24/7) - name, title, email, mobile
Who gets called at 2am when a robot is stuck or alarming. MUST be 24/7.
MBody AI technical account manager (MBody) - name, title, email, mobile
MBody-side counterpart. Customer needs to know who to call.
Billing / AR contact (fleet-wide) - name, title, email, mobile
Receives invoices. Without this, AR can't get paid on time.
Client PO approver - chargeable Break/Fix work (fleet-wide) - name, title, email, mobile
Approves chargeable estimates before work begins. Without this, chargeable WOs stall.
Client feedback / CSAT contact (per site) - name, title, email, mobile
Receives post-WO service rating requests. Drives our CSAT score.
Defective parts collection contact (per site) - name, title, email, mobile
Coordinates Cenobot OEM defective part handover. 30-day deadline.
Tells Orchestrator who is reachable when. Required for severity-based alert routing.
Default 24/7 as dummy until customer confirms.
Determines how reporting access is filtered.
Required before loading personal contact data into Orchestrator.
Who sees all-robot, all-site data. Usually executive sponsor, ops director, finance.
Who sees only their own site or sub-location.
Who can amend robot schedules / settings?
Permission control. Programme Manager fleet-wide; Site Manager own-site only is common.
Determines auth setup. Per prior session: no SSO at this time.
Default to individual email login Q1; revisit Q2 if customer raises SSO.
Reporting access scope (all robots / by zone / by team)
Critical for filtering. Drives Orchestrator role config.
Push, email, SMS - which priority gets which channel.
Default: email all priorities, SMS for Critical only.
Named on-call list for after-hours Critical events. MUST exist before go-live.
When Low/Medium alerts are silenced. Critical always on.
Some sites need silent mode (e.g. hospitals, VIP areas).
Who gets the cost estimate notification before chargeable work starts.
Which events fire which priority. Default matrix exists.
Escalation chain by severity (who escalates to whom)
If first responder doesn't ack within X minutes, who's next.
Cannot dummy - real chain needed for Critical.
Integration required? (Required / In scope / Not required)
Top-of-section gate. Default Not required Q1 per prior session.
Default Not required Q1; revisit Q2.
Identity provider (Azure AD, Okta, Google, ADFS)
Required to register Orchestrator app inside customer's IdP.
How IdP groups map to Orchestrator roles.
Top-of-section gate. Default Not required Q1.
Which work order system the customer runs.
How Orchestrator authenticates to customer's CMMS.
Mapping of robot events to CMMS work orders.
Task priority mapping (Orchestrator severity to CMMS priority)
Where tickets land inside customer's system.
Completion status sync back to Orchestrator?
Top-of-section gate. Some properties require elevator integration.
Tim owns elevator integration scoping per prior session.
Determines whether integration is even possible.
Access control / door system (Genetec, Lenel, HID, Brivo)
Many casino back-of-house areas need credentialed access.
How Orchestrator authenticates to elevator/door system.
Per-site list of where robots need to ride elevators.
Per-site list of doors robots need to traverse.
Failover behaviour (what robot does if integration fails)
Safety/UX requirement. Default: robot waits at landing and alerts site manager.
Owner of the elevator/access system on the customer side.
Additional platforms requested? (BI, BMS, Teams, Slack)
Catch-all. Most common: Power BI / Tableau for analytics.
Per prior session: ask Q1, execute Q2.
Integration purpose (what data flows where, why)
Forces customer to articulate the use case.
Integration method (API / webhook / embedded dashboard / data feed)
Defines our service obligations. MUST match the signed contract.
Already in contract - confirm in Q1.
SLA service credit rate ($70/hr/robot or negotiated)
What we owe customer if we miss SLA.
Break/Fix approval method (email / portal / signature / verbal+email)
Named approver and how fast they respond.
Client portal access for live WO visibility?
Some customers want live WO status visibility; others don't.
WO service report delivery (recipients on WO close)
Who gets the auto-generated service report when a WO closes.
Whether customer participates in post-WO satisfaction ratings.
Damage classification process (who verifies damage type)
Three damage types affect billing: Employee, Guest, Third-Party.
Standard PM cycle. Customer can request different cadence.
Who receives written PM completion report.
Standard process as dummy; real contact required.
Who is on-site for commissioning of new robots.
Which modules appear in the report (Smart Text, KPI Grid, Area by Day, Breakeven, etc.).
Standard 10 components - this IS the dummy report per prior session.
Which KPIs appear in the per-site report.
Daily / weekly / monthly cadence per site.
Default: daily email + weekly PDF + monthly deep-dive.
Who at the site gets the insight report.
Preferred report format (email / dashboard / PDF / BI feed)
Client BI / reporting tool integration (Power BI, Tableau)
Whether customer wants raw data feed for their own BI.
Benchmarking preference (vs other sites / industry / prior period)
What the customer wants to compare against.
Sales sends dummy report pre-deploy and walks customer through it.
This IS the dummy step per prior session.
+2 week post-deploy validation: real data matches expectations?
Scheduled call with CS team 2 weeks after go-live.
Insight report KPI targets need adjustment? (post-deploy)
Once 2 weeks of real data is in, customer often realises targets need tuning.
Auto-detect from property address as dummy.
For customers with properties in multiple time zones.
Defines what counts as 'business hours' for SLA clock and report scheduling.
When the daily shift-handover summary lands.
When the weekly performance summary lands.
Monthly report date & time (default 1st of month 08:00)
When the monthly review pack lands.
When robots start cleaning and when they dock.
Default 12:00am start / 12:00am dock per prior session.
Facility map (with time-of-day restrictions by area and go / no-go zones)

Source of truth for routing, scheduling, and zone design. Time-of-day overlays tell Orchestrator when each area is reachable (e.g. casino floor closed to robots 6am-2am). Go / no-go zones bake in regulator and customer restrictions before Day 1 so robots never operate where they shouldn't.
Cannot dummy. Day 1 mapping walkthrough builds on this. Overlaps with section 3 floor plan field but adds the time and access overlay.
Drives Orchestrator reporting access tiers, escalation chain, and alert routing. Without it we cannot filter dashboards correctly or know who escalates to whom when a P1 fires.
Can scaffold from contact list as dummy; real org chart preferred for clean access setup.
AR setup. Without it MBody cannot invoice. Often a procurement bottleneck on the customer side so collect this early - same risk as the contract itself.
Cannot dummy. Common deployment delay if not captured up front.
Confirm Orchestrator has APIs for the robot models customer will use. BLOCKER if missing.
New requirement — not explicit in original
If existing, skip access setup, contacts collection If new, collect Client and Client Location
If existing, reuse access controls, contact roster, reporting hierarchy If new,capture Client and Location

Sub-groupings for reporting and/or access control?

Existing — promote to top-level Y/N gate
